column1: # Days on which the source says a cumulative's movement holds records that
# belong to EARLIER days, in the source's own words.
# What an entry asserts. On this report date the national cumulative moved by
# more (or less) than the count the report states for the day itself, AND the
# report says why: a harmonisation, an integration of provincial books, a
# retrospective attachment. An entry is a claim about the document, quoted
# below, and never an inference from the size of a difference.
# What it is used for. `build_streams.py` publishes the `cases_excluding_backlog`
# and `deaths_excluding_backlog` families: the differenced daily series with the
# rows named here replaced by the report's own same-day count. Every other
# disagreement between the two readings is left alone, because the source does
# not say those records belong to other days -- most are reclassifications
# between zones or provinces, where the differenced value is the right count.
# Why a register and not a rule in code. Which days these are is a reading of
# the documents, not a property of the numbers. A threshold on the difference
# would have caught 2026-07-22 and also caught eight zone reclassifications
# that are not backlogs at all, and would have missed 2026-08-02, whose
# difference is 10.
# Scope. Both scope columns do real work and neither can be dropped.
# `quantity` is `cases`, `deaths`, or `both`. On 2026-08-02 the source
# attributes the deaths difference and says nothing about the cases one,
# which differs by 4 in the other direction and is left alone.
# `places` is the file stems the entry licenses, and it is the source's own
# scope rather than wherever the numbers happen to differ. The 22 July
# footnote names Ituri and Nord-Kivu; Haut-Uélé's readings that day also
# differ, by one case and one death, and those are NOT covered -- the source
# does not say they belong to earlier days, so they stay at the differenced
# value. `national` is listed explicitly because the tile the footnote hangs
# off is the national one.
# Beyond these two columns the substitution still applies only where both
# readings exist, the differenced row covers exactly one day, and the two
# disagree, so an entry can never silently alter a row they already agree on.
# The records dropped from the likelihood by each entry are counted in
# `meta.json` under the excluding-backlog streams, and stated in the release
# notes. Nothing here is a re-dating: the source never says which earlier days
# these records belong to, so they are excluded rather than moved.
date

column7: *Harmonisation de données avec les provinces de l'Ituri et du Nord-Kivu à la date du 22 juillet 2026.
